Coarsened exact matching defines explicit frequency bins and retains strata containing both targets and eligible donors. For heavy-tailed item counts, a practical adaptation is prespecified log-spaced bins, quantile bins with documented tie handling, or nearest-neighbor matching under |log(1+f_target)−log(1+f_donor)|≤δ. These are design choices, not universal thresholds. Record training-only frequency definitions, bin edges, boundary conventions, caliper units, eligibility rules, seed and tie-breaking; assess sensitivity to alternative widths. [MatchIt CEM documentation](https://kosukeimai.github.io/MatchIt/reference/method_cem.html)

Assess common support through target/donor frequency distributions and eligible-donor counts per target, including zero-donor rates by category and frequency bin. Check balance before and after matching using matching-weighted standardized mean differences, variance ratios, empirical-CDF differences and distribution plots for frequency and observed history covariates. Inspect raw and log frequencies because tail imbalance can survive mean balance. Absolute SMD<0.1 is a common diagnostic guideline, not proof of exchangeability; balance-test p-values are discouraged. [Balance guidance](https://kosukeimai.github.io/MatchIt/articles/assessing-balance.html)

With replacement, retain donor IDs and reuse counts, incorporate matching multiplicities in weights, and account for dependence from reused donors when estimating uncertainty. Report unique donors, reuse concentration and effective sample size. For reproducible perturbations, save every target–donor assignment and failed-match reason. Report attempted, matched and excluded users/replicates, stratified by category and frequency; compare retained versus excluded observed covariates. Exclusion changes the target to the matchable subset: these comparisons describe selection but cannot identify bias from unobserved differences. Avoid generalizing matched-subset effects to all users without additional assumptions. [Matching weights](https://kosukeimai.github.io/MatchIt/reference/matchit.html), [estimands and uncertainty](https://kosukeimai.github.io/MatchIt/articles/estimating-effects.html)
